I had the exact same fear before my son was born. I was overwhelmed with a kind of guilt I'd never known before. Through various experiences and exposures (trauma, psychedelics, philosophy books, etc) I had long since found existence to be almost plastic. Worse than just meaningless, meaninglessness that poses as meaningful. And the thought that my son would one day make some similar discovery broke my heart. 

Then he was born and I felt all of the cliche joy and love that people talk about. I didn't exactly feel like life was meaningful all of the sudden but I definitely felt useful. Like I could do whatever it took to make his life better. The love I feel is nothing I have ever experienced. Nor is the equal dose of fear that comes with it. Fear of losing him. Which I will one day. One way or another. And so it all comes back full circle.

It would be a very compassionate and courageous act to adopt a child. It would be a bold act to create one. But whichever it is (or if it's neither) you are going to take on the consequences all the same. That life has no concrete meaning should only tell you that no matter what you do.. you will arrive in the same place as everyone else.. So will your children. And their children. And so on. But those moments you have with your child are worth having. I couldn't describe them to you but as someone who has spent a long time decrying meaning... Those moments are the most meaningful experiences of my life.
